extracted.intended_audience: USPTO personnel (patent examiners and PTAB judges), patent practitioners, and the public
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating patent claims for subject matter eligibility under 35 U.S.C. §101 following the USPTO's current framework as incorporated in the MPEP. Includes use of illustrative examples, AI-specific updates, memoranda on practice, and supporting materials to apply the guidance in fact-specific situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate claims for subject matter eligibility under 35 U.S.C. 101
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO guidance explains how USPTO personnel, including patent examiners and PTAB administrative patent judges, should evaluate claims for patent subject matter eligibility under 35 U.S.C. 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO's current eligibility guidance is found in Section 2103 through 2106.07 of the Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP). Apply that guidance when deciding whether claims recite patent-eligible subject matter under the governing law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use MPEP sections 2103–2106.07 as the controlling internal standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (Sections 2103–2106.07) contains the USPTO's current eligibility guidance incorporated for examiner and PTAB use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because rejections are based on the substantive law, incorporation of the USPTO's guidance into the MPEP does not affect pending eligibility rejections or create new grounds of rejection. Rely on the stated MPEP sections as the operative internal guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use illustrative Examples (Examples 1–49) to inform fact-specific SME analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets of example claim analyses (Examples 1–49) are provided as teaching tools to assist understanding of how the USPTO applies its eligibility guidance in particular fact-specific situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Examples illustrate exemplary SME analyses across a range of technologies. Analyses issued prior to the current guidance (Examples 1–36) still provide useful illustrations; all claims indicated as eligible in these examples remain eligible under current guidance. See the index of examples for relevance under current guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply the 2024 AI SME Update for AI-related subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2024 Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance Update, including guidance specific to artificial intelligence, is part of current USPTO guidance (effective July 17, 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating claims involving AI or machine learning, incorporate the AI-specific aspects of the 2024 update (e.g., Examples 47–49 and accompanying explanations) as they reflect current USPTO practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow memoranda and best practices (e.g., for Rule 132 SMEDs) when handling procedural submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO issues memoranda and best-practices guidance that affect how practitioners submit and how examiners treat certain procedural items related to SME (e.g., Rule 132 Subject Matter Eligibility Declarations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on the page include: Memorandum - Best Practices for Submission of Rule 132 Subject Matter Eligibility Declarations (SMEDs) (Apr 30, 2026) (superseding Dec 4, 2025 memo), Advance notice of change in light of Ex Parte Desjardins (Dec 5, 2025), Memorandum to the Patent Examining Corps - Subject Matter Eligibility Declarations (Dec 4, 2025), and Reminders on evaluating subject matter eligibility (Aug 4, 2025). Follow the instructions and best practices in these memoranda when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use supporting materials (training, form paragraphs, FAQs, sample rejections, court decision chart)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO provides additional documents—training materials, form paragraphs, FAQs, a sample rejection, and a chart of subject matter eligibility court decisions—to assist consistent application of the guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage these materials as practical aids: training materials for examiner instruction, form paragraphs for consistent office action language, FAQs for clarifications, sample rejection for formatting/content expectations, and the court decisions chart for jurisprudential context. Note that some resources were posted Jan 8, 2019 and may be superseded; verify currency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely only on current, incorporated guidance; do not rely on pre-Revision 10.2019 eligibility guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility-related guidance issued prior to the Ninth Edition, Revision 10.2019 of the MPEP (revised June 2020) should not be relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View past guidance by date of issuance if needed, but be aware that guidance incorporated into the MPEP supersedes older documents; only current MPEP-incorporated guidance should govern examiner practice.
